### 6.8 M4 Adapter expansion: tasks

*Proposed breakdown (2026-10-13, Delegated agent work, documentation only; not owner-approved), written under §9.1
step 2 from the M4 row in §6 and the requirements it lists.* M4 depends on M3 and M9, both `Partial`; under §9.1 step 1
agents may start the tasks below whose dependencies need neither the operator nor zemdregon. Design:
[TDD §4](design/TDD.md#4-provider-adapter-strategy) (every M4 provider row reads "to be verified in M4"),
[TDD §5](design/TDD.md#5-implementation-strategy-by-milestone), [LLD §2](design/LLD.md#2-adapter-contract),
[LLD §6](design/LLD.md#6-compliance-manifest), [ADR-0002](adr/0002-mcp-upstream-acp-downstream.md) (ACP downstream),
[ADR-0009](adr/0009-version-gated-adapters.md), [ADR-0026](adr/0026-per-run-tool-channel-socket-and-token.md),
[ADR-0029](adr/0029-claude-code-receives-tool-shim-via-mcp-config.md) and
[ADR-0033](adr/0033-claude-channel-bypass-only-without-safe-mode.md). Provider facts come from [R2] (the
[verified research](research/headless-ai-coding-controller-verified-2026-10-12.md); "L" numbers below are its lines)
and, for Muse Code, the [research note](research/muse-code-2026-10-13.md). Every one is **Unverified** against an
installed CLI (R-7, R-33): no task may state a flag, event shape, model name, limit or price that its spike did not
source, and where the research is silent the task is to find the fact, not to assume it.

**Facts the breakdown relies on (checked against `main` at `81d7ffe`, 2026-10-13).**

- NFR-MAINT-01 is not met yet: adding an adapter today also edits `ProviderId` in `src/adapters/types.ts` (it lacks
  `muse`, which [LLD §2](design/LLD.md#2-adapter-contract) lists), `PROVIDER_IDS` in `src/config/schema.ts` (it lacks
  `muse-code`), `CONFIG_TO_ADAPTER_ID` in `src/routing/collect.ts`, the registrations in `src/cli/serve.ts` and
  `src/cli/doctor.ts`, the exports in `src/adapters/index.ts` and the single `BYPASS_FLAGS` list in
  `src/adapters/audit.ts`.
- No ACP transport exists: `Transport` names `acp-stdio`, but nothing in `src/exec/` speaks ACP and every adapter's
  `parseEvent` ignores non-string input.
- No `adapters` command exists (`src/cli/main.ts`); versions are recorded by reviewed manifest edits (Q-12), and the
  FR-ADP-02 step 7 smoke test is skipped (§6.2.1).
- CI runs on `ubuntu-24.04` only (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `src/exec/supervisor.ts` (process-tree enumeration) and
  `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` (the start-tick PID-reuse guard, LLD §8) read `/proc`, which is Linux-only, and every
  profile is ineligible on `darwin` (`SANDBOX_DEPENDENT_PROFILES`, Q-35).
- The usage ledger already stores `harness` and `backing_provider` (`src/ledger/repo.ts`, `src/usage/observations.ts`)
  and `ProbeResult.modelsListed` exists, but there is no model registry (FR-ADP-05).
- Reusable pieces: the conformance harness (`src/adapters/conformance.ts`, `REQUIRED_CASE_KINDS`), the replay-fixture
  pattern (the one shared helper `src/adapters/fixtures/replay.mjs` with a per-provider dialect in
  `src/adapters/fixtures/replay-dialects/`, and `cases.ts` under `src/adapters/claude/fixtures/` and
  `src/adapters/codex/fixtures/`; T4.3), the controller leg and the per-adapter leg of the malicious-fixture suite
  (`test/malicious/`, `test/malicious/adapters/`), the opt-in live smoke script (`scripts/live-smoke.mjs` with its
  provider plug-ins in `scripts/live/providers/`) and the `GitCapabilities` declaration (`src/adapters/types.ts`).

**Conventions for every provider group (Proposed, Delegated).**

- Groups are numbered by tens: Grok Build T4.20 to T4.29, Antigravity T4.30 to T4.39, Cursor T4.40 to T4.49, OpenCode
  T4.50 to T4.59, Kimi Code T4.60 to T4.69, Muse Code T4.70 to T4.79. In each, `T4.n0` is a documentation-only spike,
  `T4.n1` and `T4.n8` are **operator-only** (an installed CLI with the operator's native login, like T3.9 and T9.4b),
  and the rest run on fakes and synthetic fixtures in CI. Shared groundwork is T4.1 to T4.12 (no T4.0: by this
  roadmap's convention `.0` is a spike, and M4's spikes are per provider).
- A new manifest starts with a range that admits no version (`<0.0.0`, as Codex had until Q-12), so the adapter fails
  the version gate with `ADAPTER_VERSION_UNVERIFIED` until a version passes `adapters validate` (T4.4).
- Git declarations start at the fail-closed values: `gitWriteControl.kind` `none-documented` unless the spike sources a
  deny control, and `commitChannel` `finalize-only` (FR-GIT-09; owner decision 36: the controller commits at FINALIZING
  when the project opts in). An `injected` channel needs its own ADR on the ADR-0029 and ADR-0033 pattern, an operator
  opt-in and a live check; none is planned here.
- No bypass-class flag is emitted outside an approved `privileged` scope that sets bypass (FR-POL-03, ADR-0017). Each
  spike lists its provider's bypass-class flags, and T4.1 puts them in the argv audit. An approved bypass scope compiles
  on a `host` project even where the provider's Git-write control is `none-documented` or denial is not shown to hold
  under its bypass mode, relying on FR-GIT-03 and FR-GIT-06 (owner decision 46, answering Q-58); the cell is
  `Ineligible` only for a different reason, such as undocumented bypass flags.
- Synthetic fixtures are labelled synthetic and replaced by scrubbed captures from the operator task (no credential,
  token, account identifier or private prompt text).

The other 4 are equivalent (`classifyCommon` re-reads `exit.outcome` for timeout and cancel, an `exited` outcome with a null code is never expected, and the parser never binds an empty id). A second mutation pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines, parser unchanged; "antigravity parser residuals, second pass" in the same file) pins 6 more non-equivalent survivors: tool steps with no `result` end `no result event`, not a trailing tool; success needs the exit code in `expectedExitCodes`; the id is read only from the outer `init.conversation_id` and `result.conversation_id`; usage on a second `result` is never recorded even when the first had none, and a failed envelope still records its usage once (FR-CAP-01); `resumeArgs` returns the Q-86 refusal even where `compile` refuses for its own reason. Parameter shadowing closed (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines, no new capture; "antigravity tool parameters cannot shadow a command (T4.33, synthetic shapes)" in `antigravity.test.ts`): `#toolStep` now reads every parameter container (`tool_info.parameters`, `args`, `input`, then the step's own) and every Assumption key, skipping empty and non-string values, and reports each distinct command to the tool-call guard (paths only when no command is named), so an empty, non-string or benign `command`, or a container without one, no longer hides a Git write under `CommandLine` or in a later container (each such stream now ends `PERMISSION_BLOCKED`; the old parser fails these tests); the precedence above now orders the reports instead of dropping lower-precedence values. This does not touch gap (3) below or the non-`tool` step gap. A third mutation pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines only, parser unchanged; "antigravity parser residuals, third pass" in `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts`, mirroring Grok Build T4.23's fourth pass; seven one-line adapter mutations each turn at least one test red): a `result` line with no string `status` is a counted `unknown` line that does not take the result slot, so a later `result` is the first and its usage counts once; zero counters are recorded `provider_reported` and a zero total still fails (Q-86); a command is never clipped, so a Git write past the 512-character target limit reaches the tool-call guard whole and ends `PERMISSION_BLOCKED`; a parameterless tool step is reported bare once and an update naming nothing new emits nothing, while a command added to a step that reported a path is reported; a repeated `init` with the bound id emits nothing. Pinned gaps, not fixed: an `init` id that is not one safe token binds nothing, so the `result` envelope's different id becomes the bound id of a run that ends `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL_ERROR` (fixture `unsafe_then_good_result.jsonl` replays this through the supervisor, outside the T4.35 case list; with no `init`, an unsafe first `result` leaves the id to a second one); a `step_update` for another conversation before anything binds, or with a non-string `conversation_id`, is never compared, so it does not fail the run. A fourth pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines only; "antigravity parser residuals, fourth pass: event order and provider_reported usage" in `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts`, mirroring the Grok Build, Cursor and OpenCode event-order and usage residuals; each test is checked through `usageObservationsFromEvents` and four one-line adapter mutations each turn one red) closes one gap: the Q-86 total is now read as an own property of the recorded counters (`ownProp(metrics, "total_tokens")` in `adapter.ts`), so a `total_tokens` inherited from `Object.prototype` no longer turns a `SUCCESS` envelope with no reported total into a success (the old parser fails that test); counters are already read as own keys, and a JSON `__proto__` key in `usage` is never a counter. It pins the event order of one `result` line (a `result` with no `init` emits `session_bound` with its model before its usage, so the usage row carries that model; an unsafe id emits `provider_error`, usage, message, result, and the line's model reaches no usage row; a failed envelope emits usage, denials, its error, message, result, and the denial outranks the error), that a failed first `result` records its usage once and a later success cannot flip it (`more than one result line`), and that a total alone is recorded and succeeds while components without a total are recorded with nothing summed in and fail (Q-86). Pinned gaps, not fixed (FR-CAP-01 records reported numbers as is, ADR-0007): fractional counters are recorded and a fractional total above zero succeeds; a total below the sum of its components is recorded unreconciled and succeeds; fixture `usage_unreconciled.jsonl` replays this to a success through the supervisor (outside the T4.35 case list, listed in the fixture inventory). A fifth pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines only, parser unchanged; "antigravity parser residuals, fifth pass: post-result steps, prototype values and exit codes" in `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts`, mirroring Grok Build T4.23 fifth pass; four one-line adapter mutations each turn at least one test red) pins: a new command on a step after the `result` is reported, so it ends `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL_ERROR` "tool call after the result line" (`PERMISSION_BLOCKED` under the guard for a Git write); that trailing-tool detail replaces an earlier protocol detail (a second `result`, a changed `conversation_id`) while the code stands, and a non-protocol failure keeps its own detail; prototype-named event names, step types and statuses are plain strings (a counted unknown, an ignored step, a failed status); `extractResult` accepts only the compiled expected exit code 0, so exit 3, a signal and a non-`exited` outcome fail; one command under two keys or containers is reported once. Pinned gaps, not fixed: a tool step repeated unchanged after the `result` is deduplicated per `step_index`, so the trailing-tool check sees nothing and the run succeeds (fixture `trailing_repeat_step.jsonl` replays this through the supervisor, outside the T4.35 case list, listed in the fixture inventory); a step with no numeric `step_index` or a step type other than `tool` after the `result` is no tool call, so it does not fail the run; any number is a step index (fractional and negative ones are distinct steps); a prototype-named model, backing vendor, tool name or denied action is kept as an ordinary string. A sixth pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines only, parser unchanged; "antigravity parser residuals, sixth pass: boundaries, falsy values, framing and duplicate keys" in `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts`, mirroring Grok Build T4.23 sixth pass; six one-line adapter mutations each turn one test red) pins: every clip keeps a value of exactly its limit whole and clips one character more (tool name, denied action, unknown event name and status 64, model and backing vendor 128, target 512, response 2,000); a conversation id of 256 characters binds and 257 does not, and it must start with a letter or digit; a `denied_actions` of `false`, `0`, `""` or `{}` is still one `unknown` denial (`PERMISSION_BLOCKED`) while `null` and `[]` deny nothing; an `error` of `false`, `0`, `[]` or `{}` is a non-string error field (`TOOL_FAILURE`) while `""` is none; surrounding whitespace and a trailing CR parse, a BOM line is unparseable and not counted `unknown`, and top-level JSON that is not an object is a counted `unknown` line; the run summary is the last 2,000 characters of the joined messages. Pinned gaps, not fixed (no recorded `agy` line repeats a key or carries an empty tool name, [LIVE] C4, C7): a duplicated JSON key keeps its last value, so a later `SUCCESS` status hides an earlier `ERROR` (fixture `duplicate_status_key.jsonl` replays this to a success through the supervisor, outside the T4.35 case list, listed in the fixture inventory); a step's `conversation_id` is compared exactly but never checked as a safe token, so an unsafe one is reported as a changed id (the run still fails closed); an empty `tool_info.name` shadows `tool_name`, so the call is named by the empty string. A seventh pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines only, parser unchanged; "antigravity parser residuals, seventh pass: result-only backing parity, shadowing, framing and ranking" in `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts`, mirroring Grok Build T4.23 sixth/seventh passes and Cursor T4.43 / OpenCode T4.53 residuals; seven one-line adapter mutations each turn at least one test red) pins: fixture `backing_result_only.jsonl` replays a result-only stream (no `init` line) with model and `backing_provider` through conformance (`ok: true`, id bound) and usage observation (harness `antigravity`, backing vendor `backing-g` and model `gemini-3.8-flash-high` on `provider_reported` usage, T4.6, FR-ADP-10); root snake_case `backing_provider` shadows root camelCase `backingProvider` and inner `init.backing_provider`, while inner `init.model` shadows root `model`; non-string display_name falls through to action, and multiple denials preserve order with the first denial named; command keys suppress targets in the same step, a later command-less update reports target, non-object parameter containers are ignored without shadowing, and multiple distinct commands across containers report separate shell calls that trigger the guard; model and auth error prefix checks are case-sensitive and un-trimmed (capitalised or whitespace-prefixed errors end `TOOL_FAILURE`, category `unknown`); duplicate `event` and `conversation_id` keys resolve to the last one; an empty `conversation_id` parses cleanly without binding but is refused by `resumeArgs` citing Q-86, while a foreign provider is refused citing that provider before Q-86; a trailing tool call masks `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL_ERROR` failure details ("more than one result line" becomes "tool call after the result line") but does not mask permission denials, auth errors, or guard violations; tool name fallback follows `tool_info.name` > `e.tool_name` > `e.name` > `unknown` with non-string values falling through. Pinned gaps, not fixed (Assumption: native Antigravity output reports no backing vendor, live check C4): model and backing vendor on `result` are ignored once `init` has bound the session; non-null non-string or empty-string root `backing_provider` shadows inner `init.backing_provider` leaving `backingProvider` unset; empty `init.model` shadows root `model`; non-object `denied_actions` entries (strings, numbers) fall back to tool `unknown`; empty `display_name` shadows `action` resulting in an empty tool name; an update repeating a command with a new target cannot report the target; duplicate `step_type` with `"agent_response"` second turns a tool step into an ignored step, hiding a Git write from the guard. Residual eighth pass (2026-10-15, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines, parser unchanged; [PR #468](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/468)): `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts` "eighth pass: divergent duplicate keys, trailing steps and usage drift" pins duplicate `status` keys with independent denial/error payloads (a later `SUCCESS` cannot erase those signals), last-value duplicate `usage` objects, a repeated post-result command on a fresh step index (refused) versus the same index (deduplicated), a changed post-result command reaching the Git guard, ignored step usage drift and second-result totals drifting up/down without revising the first `provider_reported` observation. Pinned gaps: a final non-string duplicate `status` makes the entire result unknown, dropping its denial and usage; duplicate usage objects replace rather than merge earlier counters; an overwritten `ERROR` without another failure signal succeeds; a second result with positive tokens still emits the misleading normalized summary `SUCCESS with no reported tokens` while the run correctly fails for multiple results. Residual ninth pass (2026-10-16, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic only, parser unchanged; [PR #475](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/475)): `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts` "ninth pass: soft-denial ordering, envelope keys and resume id parity" adds 14 cases pinning soft denial across repeated/fresh post-result tool updates in ACTIVE/DONE/ERROR states, last-value duplicate whole `result` envelopes with conflicting ids/denials/usage, duplicate scalar `total_tokens` verdict/observation parity, and matching init/result-only safe, unsafe and empty id behavior with uniform Q-86 resume refusal. Residual tenth pass (2026-10-16, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic only, parser unchanged; [PR #494](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/494)): `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts` "tenth pass: Q-86 numeric edges, denial shapes, usage ownership and trailing unknowns" adds 18 cases pinning overflowing, negative-zero and subnormal `total_tokens`, non-array `denied_actions` values beside `SUCCESS` and denial precedence, first-result usage ownership, a flag-shaped objective beside the uniform resume refusal, and unreadable lines after the result. Pinned gaps: any positive total passes Q-86; a bare-string denial loses its name; a second result's usage after a usage-less first is not recorded; a trailing status-less `result` or unknown event naming a Git write is only unknown. Status stays `Partial`. Residual eleventh pass (2026-10-16, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic only, parser unchanged; [PR #503](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/503)): `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts` "eleventh pass: envelope shapes, non-string fields, status edges and the failure tail" adds 34 cases pinning non-object lines and non-string `event`/`init`/`result` values as counted unknowns, non-string `response` and `model`, near-miss statuses, and timeout and cancellation outranking every parsed failure. Pinned gaps: a result-only stream with a non-string `conversation_id` succeeds unbound; a non-string root `backing_provider` shadows a nested one; an empty `status` fails with an empty failure detail; overflowing `step_index` values collapse to one `Infinity` step; `classifyFailure` never reads the stderr tail. Status stays `Partial`. Residual twelfth pass (2026-10-16, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic only, parser unchanged, no new fixture; [PR #515](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/515)): `src/adapters/antigravity/parser-residual.test.ts` "twelfth pass: unreadable steps, root containers, in-envelope ranking and post-result init" adds 30 cases (two one-line adapter mutations each turn tests red) pinning a non-object `tool_info` falling back to `tool_name` and the step's root containers, the root `parameters`/`args`/`input` containers carrying `CommandLine`, `file_path` and `AbsolutePath` in container and key order, a post-result `init` with another or an unsafe id failing the run, a failed status or recognised error outranking an unexpected exit code, and a denial outranking both provider errors in one envelope. Pinned gaps: a `step_update` with a non-number `step_index` or non-string `step_type` is only a counted unknown, so a Git write it names never reaches the tool-call guard and the run succeeds; `state` is never read; a string `tool_info` is never read as a name or command; inside one envelope the id's protocol error outranks an auth or model error; a whitespace-only response is kept untrimmed as the summary. Status stays `Partial`. **Not done, so not `Done`:** (1) resume is not compiled (Q-86): an unknown `--conversation` id exits 0 with `SUCCESS` in a new conversation; (2) no rate-limit, sandbox-violation or exit-3 `AGY_ERROR` shape reached stdout in the live check (the `AGY_ERROR` line is on stderr, which the adapter contract does not pass to `extractResult`), so the parser emits neither: a rate limit ends `TOOL_FAILURE`, and a sandbox violation that ends in a `SUCCESS` envelope is not detected; (3) the keys of `tool_info.parameters` were not recorded, so the `command` and path names are Assumptions and a call without them is invisible to the tool-call guard. Needs the operator: a capture of a tool step's parameters, of a rate-limited run and of a resume with a known id that shows how a resumed conversation is marked (T4.31 extension). synthetic lines, no new capture, parser unchanged; [PR #495](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/495)): `src/adapters/cursor/parser-residual.test.ts` "ninth pass: refusal-container fallback, late-init persistence and aliases, trailing clip boundary and unrecorded subtypes, resume id edges and usage key gating" pins refusal-container fallback, refusal-text regex edges, multi-key denial ordering, late-`init` persistence and session-id alias equivalence, trailing-unknown clip boundary at 64 and an unrecorded trailing `tool_call` subtype, `resumeArgs` id edges and mutation isolation, and hostile usage token shapes. **Ninth residual pass (steward squash-merge [PR #495](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/495); fakes only, parser unchanged).** Residual tenth pass (2026-10-16, Delegated, not owner-approved; synthetic lines, no new capture, parser unchanged; [PR #506](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/506)): `src/adapters/cursor/parser-residual.test.ts` "tenth pass: late session binding after result, trailing events after finish, resume argv identity and denied tool interactions" pins late session binding after an id-less `result` (fixtures `late_id_on_trailing_unknown.jsonl` and `late_id_on_trailing_tool.jsonl`), trailing-tool detail rewrite only under `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL_ERROR`, resume argv identity, and case-variant refusal keys (fixture `denied_key_case_variant.jsonl`). **Tenth residual pass (draft [PR #506](https://github.com/zemdregon/switchboard/pull/506); fakes only, parser unchanged).** **Not done, so not `Done`:** (1) no rate-limit or sandbox-violation event shape was recorded (a failed run prints no stream, live check rows 4 and 14), so the parser emits neither and such failures end `TOOL_FAILURE` on the exit code; the stderr text is not read because the adapter contract passes none to `extractResult`; (2) native Cursor CLI captures (live check row 102) report only a model display name and no vendor, and TDD §4.5 forbids deriving one from the display name, so without an explicit structured backing_provider (supported for fronted harnesses, T4.6) backingProvider stays unset. Needs the operator: a capture of a rate-limited or quota-stopped Cursor run, and of any native field naming the backing vendor if one exists (T4.41 extension). `src/adapters/fixtures/scratch-provider.ts` in `doctor`, `list_capabilities` and config validation; the T3.17 matrix
over every declared flag). Limits: Claude Code and Codex stay exported from `src/adapters/index.ts` (new adapters are
not added there); a runtime-registered id is outside the TypeScript `ProviderId` union, and the MCP dynamic-project
schema keeps the built-in config ids.

**T4.9 status note (2026-10-13, Delegated agent work, not owner-approved).** Implemented on branch `m4-macos`, not yet
merged; the macOS path was **Unverified** (written on Linux, fixtures only) until T4.10 ran it (2026-10-14: it runs on
the macOS CI leg; the `EPERM` finding is in T4.10). One platform port, `src/exec/proc-info.ts`, answers "start time of
a PID" and "does this group have a live non-zombie member": `/proc` on Linux (the M1 behaviour, moved unchanged), BSD
`/bin/ps -A` with fixed `-o` columns under `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC` on macOS (start time stored as UTC epoch seconds
from `lstart`), and nothing elsewhere. Any failure or unparseable output means "cannot verify": the orphan check
reports `unverifiable` and never signals (before, a missing `/proc` read as "leader gone"), and the cancel loop counts
the group as alive. Mechanism, sources and limits: [LLD §8.3](design/LLD.md#83-process-table-per-platform-m4-t49); TDD
§2 and the README requirements line updated. Evidence: `src/exec/proc-info.test.ts` (both parsers, grandchild by
group, zombies, PID reuse by start time, unparseable or failed `ps`, unsupported platforms) and
`src/reconcile/process.test.ts` (every orphan rule over injected Linux, macOS and unsupported tables). Further
Linux-only assumptions, listed, not fixed: the `alive()` helper in `src/exec/supervisor.test.ts` reads `/proc` and
returns false on macOS, so its child and grandchild kill checks would passed vacuously there (made portable by T4.10);
a Linux host whose `/proc` cannot be read still treats the leader as gone (M1 behaviour kept); the socket path cap of
100 bytes (`src/git/tool-protocol.ts`) is assumed to fit the macOS `sun_path` limit, which is not cited;
case-insensitive APFS volumes were not examined for path and ref comparisons; the signing tests skip without `gpg`
(T4.10 lists skips). `/dev/null`, `detached` sessions, `kill(-pgid, …)` and the data-directory lock are POSIX and need
no change.

#### 6.8.1 Order, waves and hot files

- **Wave A (agents, now; nothing needs a provider CLI):** T4.1, T4.7, T4.9 and the spikes T4.20, T4.30, T4.40, T4.50,
  T4.60 and T4.70.
- **Wave B:** T4.2, T4.3, T4.5 and T4.6 after T4.1; T4.4 after T4.3; T4.8 after T4.7; T4.10 after T4.9; each
  provider's `T4.n2` after T4.1 and its spike, in [R2]'s order (L946): Grok Build, Antigravity, Cursor, OpenCode.
  Provider groups can run in parallel because each lives in its own module directory once T4.1 is done.
- **Wave C:** `T4.n3` to `T4.n7` and `T4.n9` per provider. Kimi Code T4.62 to T4.67 and T4.69 are unblocked (B-1
  cleared 2026-10-15); Muse Code (Should) goes last.
- **Operator, whenever the CLIs are available:** T4.11, T4.12, each `T4.n1` (after its spike) and each `T4.n8`.
- **Hot files:** `src/adapters/audit.ts`, `src/adapters/registry.ts`, `src/adapters/types.ts`, `src/config/schema.ts`
  and `src/routing/collect.ts` (T4.1 only; afterwards a provider adds one registry entry); `src/exec/` (T4.8, T4.9);
  `src/adapters/conformance.ts` and `test/malicious/` (T4.3 before any `T4.n5` or `T4.n6`); `src/cli/` (T4.4);
  `docs/design/TDD.md` (each spike edits only its own §4 subsection; merge one at a time); `README.md` (`T4.n9` and
  T4.90). Tasks sharing a hot file run one after another, never in parallel (AGENTS.md).
- No code that emits a new provider's bypass-class flag lands before T4.1.

step 2 from the M5 row in §6 and the requirements it lists.* M5 depends on M4, which is `Planned`. Only T5.8 uses M4
output (each new adapter's resume); the other tasks run on the fake adapter, Claude Code and Codex, so under §9.1 step 1
agents may start them when no M4 task is available (Proposed). Design:
[ADR-0001](adr/0001-controller-owned-canonical-state.md) (controller-owned state, no transcript parsing),
[ADR-0006](adr/0006-worktree-checkpoints-no-blind-replay.md), [FRD WF-2](requirements/FRD.md#wf-2-continue-on-the-same-provider),
[FRD WF-3](requirements/FRD.md#wf-3-cross-provider-handoff), [FRD §3](requirements/FRD.md#3-business-rules) (BR-8,
BR-18, BR-40), [FRD §5](requirements/FRD.md#5-meta-session-lifecycle),
[FRD §7.2](requirements/FRD.md#72-continue_task), [HLD §6.2](design/HLD.md#62-cross-provider-handoff-wf-3),
[SDD §2](design/SDD.md#2-component-collaboration-per-workflow), [LLD §1](design/LLD.md#1-data-model),
[LLD §2](design/LLD.md#2-adapter-contract), [LLD §3](design/LLD.md#3-mcp-tool-contracts),
[LLD §5](design/LLD.md#5-workspace-and-lease-algorithm) and
[TDD §5](design/TDD.md#5-implementation-strategy-by-milestone). No LLD section defines the handoff bundle yet; T5.1

**Facts the breakdown relies on (checked against `main` at `ce40972`, 2026-10-14).**

- FR-SES-01 is done (M1). FR-SES-02 is **partly built**: `meta_session` has `objective`, `constraints_json`,
  `repo_root`, `base_commit`, `head_commit` and `open_work_json` (`src/ledger/migrations/0001_initial.ts`). Objective
  and constraints are written at creation (`src/ledger/repo.ts`), `repo_root` and `base_commit` by the workspace
  manager and `head_commit` at finalize (`src/workspace/manager.ts`). Not built: nothing writes `open_work_json`; the
  `decision` table and its append-only triggers exist (migration 0001) but no code inserts a row; changed files and
  verification results exist per run only (`changed_files` artifact, verification event and `test_report`), not as
  meta-session state; `provider_binding` rows are written (`src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts`, "FR-SES-02/03: remember the
  native session") but `recordProviderBinding` stores `harness` equal to `provider` and no backing provider or model,
  although `usage_observation` already carries both (T4.6).
- FR-SES-03 is **partly built**: `continue_task` (`continueTask` in `src/mcp/server.ts`) resumes the latest binding of
  the bound provider through the adapter's `resumeArgs` (`src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts`). `resumeArgs` exists for Claude
  Code, Codex (its form is an Assumption in `src/adapters/codex/adapter.ts`) and the fake adapter, and `resume` is one
  of the conformance suite's `REQUIRED_CASE_KINDS` (`src/adapters/conformance.ts`). Each continuation runs in a new
  worktree, `<data>/worktrees/<sess>/<run>` from the head checkpoint (`src/workspace/manager.ts`), not in the previous
  run's worktree as FRD WF-2's Proposed text says. Whether a provider's resume depends on the working directory is the
  WF-2 **Assumption**, still unchecked; the M4 spikes list it as an operator check for Antigravity
  ([TDD §4.4.3](design/TDD.md#443-t431-operator-checklist-antigravity), C9), Cursor
  ([TDD §4.5.3](design/TDD.md#453-t441-operator-checklist), item 8) and Muse Code (`--allow-workspace-switch`,
  [TDD §4.8](design/TDD.md#48-muse-code-m4)).
- FR-SES-04 is **not built**: `continueTask` refuses a different provider ("cross-provider continuation ... is not
  available yet") and a meta-session with no binding. `CompileRequest.handoff` is declared
  (`src/adapters/types.ts`) and unused. The `handoff_view` artifact kind is allowed by the ledger
  (`src/ledger/migrations/0009_pr_draft_artifact.ts`) and listed by `get_artifacts` (`src/mcp/schemas.ts`), but nothing
  writes it. The only bundle text in the LLD is the `handoff_condense` input of
  [LLD §13.6](design/LLD.md#136-task-contracts).
- FR-SES-05: `run_event` is append-only (M1); no handoff view exists.
- Only one fake provider exists (`fake`). The T4.1 runtime registration (`registerProvider` in
  `src/adapters/providers.ts`, used by `src/adapters/fixtures/scratch-provider.ts`) lets a test add a second one with no
  production source edit.

**Conventions (Proposed, Delegated).**

- T5.0 is a documentation-only spike. T5.1 is the design gate: no code that writes a bundle, a `decision` row or a
  `handoff_view` artifact lands before its ADR and LLD text merge, because the bundle is a new persisted format and
  carries one provider's reported text into another provider's prompt (AGENTS.md: persistence format and trust
  boundary).
- Every test runs on fake adapters; the second fake is registered by tests only. No task here calls a live provider
  except the operator task T5.12, which is skipped unless `SWITCHBOARD_LIVE_TESTS=1`.
- No number is invented: bundle size and excerpt bounds are configuration values whose defaults T5.1 chooses and labels
  as Assumptions.
- Until Q-61 is answered, a cross-provider continuation whose resolved profile is `privileged` is refused with
  `INVALID_REQUEST` (fail closed, Proposed default); same-provider `privileged` continuations keep FRD C7 unchanged.

#### 6.9.1 Order, waves and hot files

- **Wave A (agents, now; nothing needs a provider CLI):** T5.0 and T5.2.
- **Wave B:** T5.1 after T5.0. Q-61 is asked in the meantime; its fail-closed default lets T5.6 proceed.
- **Wave C:** T5.3 and T5.7 after T5.1; T5.4 after T5.3; T5.5 after T5.4; T5.6 after T5.2 and T5.5.
- **Wave D:** T5.9 after T5.6 and T5.7; T5.10 after T5.6; T5.11 after T5.9; T5.8 per adapter as M4's parser tasks
  land; T5.13 last.
- **Operator, whenever Claude Code and Codex are logged in:** T5.12.
- **Outside M5:** T11.10 (§6.6) waits for T5.4. M6's failover after `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (BR-8, FR-CAP-06, FR-MCP-10)
  reuses T5.4 and T5.6. In M7 a handoff requested by the orchestrator is a `user_request` affinity switch (SDD routing
  note, FR-RTE-07); M5 writes no affinity.
- **Hot files:** `src/mcp/server.ts` and `src/mcp/schemas.ts` (T5.6, T5.10); `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` (T5.3, T5.5,
  T5.7); `src/ledger/repo.ts` and `src/ledger/migrations/` (T5.3, T5.4); `src/adapters/types.ts` (T5.5, T5.7);
  `src/workspace/manager.ts` (T5.7); `docs/design/LLD.md` (T5.1); `docs/design/TDD.md` (T5.0, T5.12). Tasks sharing a
  hot file run one after another, never in parallel (AGENTS.md).

#### 6.9.2 Blocks Done: what needs the operator or zemdregon

M5 can reach `Partial` on fakes: FR-SES-02 populated, FR-SES-04, the FR-SES-05 handoff view, the acceptance test T5.9,
and FR-SES-03 for Claude Code, Codex and the fakes on fixtures. `Done` also needs:

1. **The operator:** T5.12, the "one opt-in live pair" in the M5 row's verification column, with Claude Code and Codex
   installed and logged in. The Codex resume form is an Assumption in `src/adapters/codex/adapter.ts` until the M2 live
   smoke run (§6.2 "Blocks Done" item 1) confirms it.
2. **FR-SES-03 "(all)":** each M4 adapter's resume, on fixtures through T5.8 and live through that adapter's operator
   tasks (`T4.n1`, `T4.n8`). Whether each provider's resume is tied to the working directory is Unverified until those
   captures (T5.0). Delegated reading, as in §6.8.2 item 2: M5 may be `Partial` with only the adapters M4 has not
   delivered outstanding.
3. **zemdregon:** Q-61 (a durable `privileged` approval and a continuation on another provider). Until it is answered
   the fail-closed default applies. M5's acceptance criteria involve no `privileged` run, so the answer does not block
   `Done` (Delegated reading), but T5.6 changes if the answer is "covered".
4. **Not needed for M5:** T11.10 (condensation, M11) and the failover use of the bundle (M6).

### 6.11 M6 Capacity and resilience: tasks

*Proposed breakdown (2026-10-14, Delegated agent work, documentation only; not owner-approved), written under §9.1
step 2 from the M6 row in §6 and the requirements it lists.* M6 depends on M5, which is `Partial` with only the
operator task T5.12 left, so under §9.1 step 1 agents start M6 tasks that do not need that item (Proposed). It is
numbered after §6.10 so that the M13 section keeps its anchor. Design: [ADR-0007](adr/0007-capacity-as-confidence-estimate.md)
(capacity is a confidence-weighted estimate), [ADR-0032](adr/0032-provider-model-affinity.md) (affinity; cache and
switch counts in M6, the affinity step in M7), [ADR-0006](adr/0006-worktree-checkpoints-no-blind-replay.md) (no blind
replay), [ADR-0038](adr/0038-handoff-bundle-and-continuity.md) (the bundle a failover reuses),
[FRD WF-5](requirements/FRD.md#wf-5-failure-handling-and-retry), [FRD §3](requirements/FRD.md#3-business-rules) (BR-3,
BR-6 to BR-9, BR-41, BR-45), [FRD §4](requirements/FRD.md#4-canonical-run-state-machine) (T4, T7, T16, T18),
[SDD §1](design/SDD.md#1-shared-design-patterns) (circuit breaker, bounded queue, "estimate, not authority"),
[LLD §1](design/LLD.md#1-data-model) (`usage_observation`, `provider_health`, `run.parent_run_id`, `next_attempt_at`),
[LLD §3](design/LLD.md#3-mcp-tool-contracts) (`get_capacity`), [LLD §3.2](design/LLD.md#32-provider-and-model-affinity-m7)
(FR-CAP-08 accounting), [LLD §4](design/LLD.md#4-failure-taxonomy), [LLD §9](design/LLD.md#9-retryback-off-algorithm)
and [TDD §5](design/TDD.md#5-implementation-strategy-by-milestone) (M6 row). LLD §3 says of `get_capacity` and LLD §9
says of breakers, adaptive concurrency and failover "to be detailed in M6"; T6.1 writes that.

**Facts the breakdown relies on (checked against `main` at `5531c78`, 2026-10-14).**

- FR-CAP-01 (record) is **built** (M2, T2.5): `usage_observation` rows with `source` `provider_reported` from each
  adapter's `usage` events (`src/usage/observations.ts`); `source` also allows `controller_estimated` (never written)
  and `inner_agent` (T11.5, migration 0006). The MCP envelope's `usage.estimated` and `usage.capacity_confidence` are
  always `null` (`src/mcp/envelope.ts`). Nothing reads `usage_observation` to estimate anything.
- `provider_health` exists (migration 0001: `breaker_state` `CLOSED`/`OPEN`/`HALF_OPEN`, `breaker_until`,
  `consecutive_failures`, `last_failure_code`, `capacity_json`) and **no code reads or writes it**. The only circuit
  breaker in the code is the in-memory inner-agent one (`src/inner/breaker.ts`, T11.2), which is not a provider breaker.
- FR-CAP-04 is **partly built** (M1): the bounded queue (`QUEUE_FULL` at admission, Q-5), the global limit and one
  `limits.per_provider_concurrency` value applied to every provider in `pump()` (`src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts`; defaults
  4 and 1 in `src/config/load.ts`, the NFR-PERF-03 proposed targets). No per-provider breaker; the eligibility filter
  (`src/routing/eligibility.ts`) has no circuit or capacity reason. NFR-PERF-03 "per provider" is therefore met only as
  one shared value, not a value per provider.
- FR-CAP-05 and FR-MCP-10 are **not built**: at FINALIZING the lifecycle records `retry_eligible` and `auto_retry:
  false` in the `workspace_assessment` event (`RETRYABLE` in `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` and
  `src/reconcile/reconcile.ts`); `run.parent_run_id`, `attempt` and `next_attempt_at` exist and nothing sets them for a
  retry; `WAITING_CAPACITY` is a valid state (cancel and reconciliation handle it) but no transition enters it; `get_run`
  has no successor field. The FRD's `retry_of` link has no column of that name; LLD §9 uses `parent_run_id`.
- FR-CAP-06: `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` is a failure code (LLD §4) and BR-3 maps "known quota exhaustion" to it, but nothing
  knows a quota is exhausted, nothing fails over and there is no `capacity.queue_horizon` key (named in
  [TDD §3.1](design/TDD.md#31-configuration), absent from `src/config/schema.ts`). The M5 handoff bundle and
  cross-provider `continue_task` (T5.4 to T5.6) exist and are what BR-8 failover reuses.
- Rate-limit signals: adapters emit a `rate_limit` event with an optional `resetAt` (Claude Code from
  `rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info`, `src/adapters/claude/parse.ts`; Codex and the fake adapter), stored as a bounded
  `run_event` payload with `reset_at` (`compactEvent` in `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts`). The Claude shape is an
  Assumption in that parser; no provider in the research reports remaining quota.
- Cache token counts (Q-53): reported keys seen so far are `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`
  from Grok Build 1.0.50 ([live check 4a](research/live-checks-2026-10-14-grok.md)), `cacheReadTokens` and
  `cacheWriteTokens` from Cursor CLI ([live check 5a](research/live-checks-2026-10-14-cursor.md)), and `cache.read` and
  `cache.write` in OpenCode's documented `step_finish` ([TDD §4.6](design/TDD.md#46-opencode-m4)). Codex's
  `cached_input_tokens` is in a **synthetic** fixture only (`src/adapters/codex/fixtures/success_edit.jsonl`). Claude
  Code's parser copies every numeric `usage.*` key without naming cache keys. None is normalised.
- `get_capacity`, `switchboard capacity` and a `capacity` configuration section do not exist. `providers.<id>.weight`
  exists in the schema (a number in [0, 1]) and nothing reads it (ADR-0007's "relative weight ... as a prior").
- T11.5 (§6.6) left one clause for M6: `get_capacity` and the estimator must be byte-identical with and without inner
  calls, and must read `inner_agent` rows deliberately or ignore them, never as `provider_reported`.

**Conventions (Proposed, Delegated).**

- **Fail closed on unknown capacity.** No provider reports remaining quota in any source we hold, so an estimate built
  from nothing has `capacity_score` and `explicit_remaining` `null` and `confidence` 0, and every surface shows it as
  unknown, never as headroom. `explicit_remaining` is filled only from a key the adapter declares as provider-reported
  remaining capacity, and no adapter declares one until a source shows it (FR-CAP-03). "Known quota exhaustion" for
  BR-3 and FRD T7 needs positive evidence (a `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` failure with a `reset_at` still in the future, or an
  open breaker); an unknown estimate does not make a provider ineligible, because that would make every provider
  ineligible. Where a number is needed and no source gives one (breaker threshold and cool-down, backoff, queue
  horizon), the default is the conservative value LLD §9 or NFR-PERF-03 already proposes, or the most restrictive
  sensible one, labelled an **Assumption**, and configurable.
- **No invented provider numbers.** No task states a provider's limit, price, quota, reset window or tier size. T6.0
  sources what each CLI reports; anything unsourced reads `Unverified: <operator task>`. FR-CAP-07's rate gate applies
  only to a provider whose enforceable limit for the auth mode in use is sourced, and stays off otherwise.
- **Design gate.** T6.1 (documentation only) writes the contracts before code: the estimator's inputs and output, the
  `get_capacity` and `capacity` output, the breaker and retry state, the successor link and the `capacity` config keys.
  Any new table, column or event type is specified in LLD §1 first and gets an ADR (AGENTS.md: persistence format and
  external interface).
- Every test runs on fake adapters with an injected clock and random source; no task here calls a live provider except
  the operator task T6.11, which is skipped unless `SWITCHBOARD_LIVE_TESTS=1`. Adapter code (`src/adapters/**`) is not
  edited for M6 except to declare a field T6.0 sources; normalisation of reported keys lives in the capacity module.
- M6 writes no affinity row: the `project_affinity` table, the selection step and `affinity_switch_reason` are M7
  (LLD §3.2). FR-CAP-08's kept-versus-switched counts are computed from runs and `route_decision` rows, with the reason
  `unrecorded` until M7 writes one.

#### 6.11.1 Order, waves and hot files

- **Wave A (agents, now; nothing needs a provider CLI or an owner decision):** T6.0 and T6.1 (documentation), then
  T6.2, T6.4, T6.5 and T6.9 after T6.1, and T6.3 after T6.2.
- **Wave B:** T6.6 after T6.5 and T6.2; T6.7 after T6.0 and T6.3; T6.10 after T6.3 to T6.7 and T6.9; T6.12 last.
- **Wave C (owner decision 57, 2026-10-17; agents, on fakes):** T6.13 after T6.2, T6.14 after T6.13, T6.8 (pacing gate,
  reframed) after T6.14, T6.16 after T6.8, T6.14 and T7.15. T6.15 after T6.11 and T6.13, once `src/adapters/**` is
  free. *T6.8 was `Blocked` and then `Deferred` until 2026-10-17; it no longer waits for a published limit.*
- **Operator, whenever a provider is logged in:** T6.11 (every provider since 2026-10-17; `Done` 2026-10-17 with
  `NOT_CHECKED` cells that the operator's capture hook fills in a follow-up note).
- **Outside M6:** M7 adds the affinity step and `affinity_switch_reason`; T6.6's failover is then a `capacity_exhausted`
  switch (FR-RTE-07) and T6.7's `unrecorded` reasons become recorded ones. T11.5's open clause (§6.6) closes with T6.2.
- **Hot files:** `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` (T6.4, T6.5, T6.6, T6.9; its admission redaction belongs to the Q-68
  work, which M6 does not touch); `src/routing/eligibility.ts` (T6.4, T6.6); `src/mcp/server.ts` and
  `src/mcp/schemas.ts` (T6.3, T6.5; the HTTP transport, OAuth and Origin code in `src/mcp/http.ts` is M13's and is not
  edited); `src/config/schema.ts` and `src/config/load.ts` (T6.2, T6.4, T6.9); `src/reconcile/reconcile.ts` (T6.5);
  `docs/design/LLD.md` (T6.1). M6 does not edit TDD §4 (M4's). Tasks sharing a hot file run one after another, never in
  parallel (AGENTS.md).

#### 6.11.2 Blocks Done: what needs the operator or zemdregon

M6 can reach `Partial` on fakes: the estimator, `get_capacity` and `capacity`, the breaker, retry with successors, the
quota ladder, per-provider limits and the acceptance test T6.10. `Done` also needs:

1. **The operator:** T6.11, so that the rate-limit, quota and usage shapes of every provider are checked (generalised
   2026-10-17); until then the retry, quota and pacing paths are proven on fakes and synthetic fixtures only, and
   pacing runs on operator-declared budgets labelled `controller_estimated`.
   *2026-10-17:* T6.11 is `Done` with `NOT_CHECKED` cells: every capture so far is text mode, so the adapters' stream
   limit shapes are still synthetic, and Grok Build and Muse Code have none
   ([limit captures 2026-10-17](research/limit-captures-2026-10-17.md)).
2. **Sources for provider facts:** which CLIs report cache counts (Q-53) and whether any provider publishes an
   enforceable limit for its subscription login (FR-CAP-07). Without a source, cache figures stay absent for that
   provider; the pacing gate (T6.8 since 2026-10-17) needs no published limit, only declared windows. Neither blocks
   the M6 acceptance criteria (Delegated reading).
3. **zemdregon:** nothing in this breakdown changes what a bypass run may do, so no owner question is opened. A retry or
   failover of a `privileged` run follows the M5 rule: a failover to another provider is the cross-provider case of
   Q-61 and is refused while Q-61 is open (fail closed), and a same-provider retry runs under the approval as is.
4. **Not needed for M6:** the M7 affinity step (`project_affinity`, `affinity reset`, the replay test).

### 6.12 M7 Routing: tasks

*Proposed breakdown (2026-10-14, Delegated agent work, documentation only; not owner-approved), written under §9.1
step 2 from the M7 row in §6 and the requirements it lists.* M6 is `Partial`; T6.11 is `Done`
(2026-10-17) and the remaining items are the wave C tasks (T6.8 reframed, `Done` 2026-10-17, and T6.16, `Done` 2026-10-17;
T6.13, T6.14 and T6.15 `Done`) and `NOT_CHECKED` follow-up cells, so under §9.1 step 1 agents start M7 tasks
that do not need them. It is
numbered after §6.11 so that
earlier anchors stay. Design: [ADR-0008](adr/0008-two-stage-routing.md) (two-stage routing: hard filter, then static
weighted score, every decision persisted), [ADR-0032](adr/0032-provider-model-affinity.md) (provider and model affinity,
owner decision 40), [ADR-0043](adr/0043-capacity-estimate-breaker-and-retry.md) (the capacity estimate, breaker and
retry M7 reads), [ADR-0007](adr/0007-capacity-as-confidence-estimate.md), [FRD §3](requirements/FRD.md#3-business-rules)
(BR-1 to BR-5, BR-39, BR-45), [LLD §1](design/LLD.md#1-data-model) (`route_decision`), [LLD §3](design/LLD.md#3-mcp-tool-contracts)
(`explain_route`, "to be detailed in M7"), [LLD §3.2](design/LLD.md#32-provider-and-model-affinity-m7) (affinity table,
algorithm, decision fields, events), [LLD §13.6](design/LLD.md#136-task-contracts) (`route_features` shape and the
per-feature `source`), [LLD §16](design/LLD.md#16-capacity-and-resilience-m6) (the estimate), [TDD §3.1](design/TDD.md#31-configuration)
(`routing.weights`), [TDD §3.13.3](design/TDD.md#3133-testing-affinity-and-retrieval) (affinity replay) and
[TDD §5](design/TDD.md#5-implementation-strategy-by-milestone) (M7 row).

**Facts the breakdown relies on (checked against `main` at `55e3d4b`, 2026-10-14).**

- Stage 1 is **built** (M2 T2.3, extended by T3.7, T6.4 and T6.6): `filterEligible` in `src/routing/eligibility.ts` is
  pure, and `collectFacts` in `src/routing/collect.ts` gathers the facts. Its reasons cover enablement, client ceiling,
  platform, binary and probe, manifest and version gate, auth, the adapter's compile verdict per profile,
  `PROFILE_PLATFORM_UNVERIFIED`, `CIRCUIT_OPEN` and `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED_KNOWN`. Not modelled: `minimum_capability` (the
  MCP server refuses it with `ELIGIBILITY_NONE`, "no model registry", in `checkRouting`, `src/mcp/server.ts`, although
  the T4.5 model registry now exists), required tools and sandbox strength as separate constraints, and concurrency,
  which queues rather than excludes (Q-5).
- **There is no stage 2.** `selectProvider` in `src/mcp/server.ts` picks `provider_preference` if it is eligible, else
  the first eligible provider in configured order (BR-4's M2 tie-break), and `routeRecord` stores the basis as
  `selection.basis`. `toRouteDecisionJson` writes `features_json` (request facts: candidates, required provider,
  profiles, requirements, platform), `candidates_json` (per provider: eligible and reasons), `weights_json` `NULL` and
  no score. `continue_task` (BR-18) and the lifecycle's quota failover (`submitFailover`, T6.6) write their own route
  decisions with `selection` and `continuation` objects.
- No heuristic classifier (FR-RTE-04), no `routing` configuration section (`src/config/schema.ts` has none, though TDD
  §3.1 names `routing.weights`), no `explain_route` tool, no `project_affinity` table and no `routing_affinity_*` event.
  The newest migration is `0013_http_subject.ts`, so the next is 0014. `delegate_task` takes no `model` argument
  (`src/mcp/schemas.ts`), so "an explicit model in the request" (FR-RTE-07, 08) cannot occur yet.
- M6 left hooks for M7: the capacity projection (`src/capacity/projection.ts`) gives per provider `throttle_risk`,
  `capacity_score` (`null` when unknown, Q-69) and `confidence`; T6.7's `switchCounts` (`src/capacity/cache.ts`) reads
  `reasons_json.affinity.affinity_switch_reason` and counts `unrecorded` until M7 writes one; the retry chain records
  `retry_not_scheduled` with `attempts_exhausted` (FR-CAP-05) and the quota ladder records `quota_failover`.
- No source gives a provider's price, a model ranking, a quality score or a sandbox-strength order (T6.0's
  [capacity-signals note](research/capacity-signals-2026-10-14.md) found no price or limit for the logins in use).
  The controller's own ledger holds run outcomes and durations per provider.
- The prompt each adapter sends is assembled inside the adapter (`promptText` in `src/adapters/claude/adapter.ts`, and
  the handoff renderer in `src/continuity/render.ts`), so FR-RTE-09 touches adapter code.

**Conventions (Proposed, Delegated).**

- **No invented provider facts.** A score term whose per-provider value has no source (monetary cost, security risk, any
  model ranking) takes the same neutral value for every candidate, so it can never decide a route, and each weight
  default is documented, configurable and an **Assumption**. Terms computed from the controller's own ledger (success
  rate and latency over the capacity window, the M6 estimate, handoff cost) are facts, not claims.
- **Unknown capacity is never headroom (Q-69).** A `null` `capacity_score` scores as the worst capacity risk, never as
  spare capacity, and never makes a provider ineligible on its own.
- **Fail closed, keep the provider.** Where the switch logic is unsure (a missing affinity row field, an estimate below
  the configured confidence, an unset low-water mark), affinity holds; where routing cannot decide (no candidate), the
  request is refused with the BR-3 code, as today. Replay never calls a model or a provider: it reads stored features.
- **Design gate.** T7.0 (documentation only) writes the contracts before code: the feature set, the score, the decision
  record, `explain_route`, the `routing` configuration section, the affinity data and the reset command. A new table,
  column or event type is specified in the LLD first and is covered by an ADR (AGENTS.md).
- Every test runs on fake adapters with an injected clock; no task calls a live provider. Routing code lives in
  `src/routing/`; edits to `src/mcp/server.ts` are limited to calling it and to the `explain_route` tool, and
  `src/adapters/**` is not edited while the M4 adapter work holds it.

- **Wave A (agents, now; nothing needs a provider CLI or an owner decision):** T7.0 first (documentation), then T7.1
  and T7.4 after it, T7.2 after T7.1, T7.3 after T7.2, T7.5 after T7.2 and T7.4, T7.6 after T7.5, T7.7 after T7.5.
- **Wave B:** T7.10 after T7.3 and T7.5 to T7.7; T7.11 last (both done). T7.8 is blocked on T7.12 (its row).
- **Wave C (owner decision 57, 2026-10-17; agents, on fakes):** T7.13 after T7.1, T7.14 after T7.13, T7.15 after T7.14
  and T6.13, T7.16 after T7.15, T7.17 after T7.16 and T6.16. A Codex member stays excluded with `CAPABILITY_MISSING`
  until a Codex model flag is sourced (Q-11, R-68); that does not block any task.
- **Waits for another lane:** T7.9 edits adapter prompt assembly, so it starts after the M4 adapter work releases
  `src/adapters/**` (§6.8.1); T7.12 (model pinning, added by T7.5) needs an adapter-contract field from the same lane.
- **Hot files:** `src/mcp/server.ts` (T7.2, T7.3, T7.5; only the routing call sites and the `explain_route` tool, never
  the HTTP transport); `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` (T7.2 and T7.5: the failover decision and the success hook);
  `src/config/schema.ts` and `src/config/load.ts` (T7.1, T7.4); `src/ledger/repo.ts` (T7.2, T7.4); `docs/design/LLD.md`
  (T7.0). Tasks sharing a hot file run one after another, never in parallel (AGENTS.md).

#### 6.12.2 Blocks Done: what needs the operator or zemdregon

M7 can reach `Done` on fakes; no task needs a provider login (Delegated reading: the acceptance criteria are all
replay, property and fault-injection tests). Open items that do not block it:

1. **zemdregon, optional:** Q-51 (stay on the new provider after a capacity switch) and Q-52 (no idle expiry) are
   Delegated defaults that M7 implements as written; zemdregon may revise them. The default weights and the
   `low_water_mark` and `min_confidence` defaults are T7.0's Delegated Assumptions. Nothing here changes what a bypass
   run may do: affinity never moves a `privileged` meta-session to another provider (the Q-61 rule stays in force).
2. **Sources for provider facts:** a price, model ranking or sandbox-strength order per provider. Without one the
   matching term stays neutral and `minimum_capability` needs an operator-declared capability (T7.8).
3. **Another lane:** T7.9 and T7.12 wait for `src/adapters/**` (T7.12: Q-90).

### 6.13 M14 Control plane: tasks

*Proposed breakdown (2026-10-15, Delegated agent work, documentation only; not owner-approved), written from the M14 row
in §6 and the requirements it lists.* Owner decision 49 sets the milestone and its place after M2's live checks;
decisions 50 to 52 set its approval-proxy, channel and CAP-16 answers. Requirements: [SRS
§3.17](requirements/SRS.md#317-control-plane-fr-ctl) (FR-CTL-01 to 11) and [PRD
CAP-15](requirements/PRD.md#3-capabilities). Design records: [ADR-0047](adr/0047-approval-proxy-over-mcp.md) and
[ADR-0048](adr/0048-notification-sinks.md), both Proposed; the discovery note, §5 and §6 (recommendations 1 to 5, 9 and
10).
**Facts the breakdown relies on (discovery note §3, checked on `main` at `066a03c`; not re-checked for this change).**

- The MCP server advertises tools only and has no tool that lists runs or reports changes since a point in time.
`get_run` is the only per-run read (`src/mcp/server.ts`).
- Approval is given only through the operator CLI (`approve`, `deny`, `projects approve`; FR-OPS-02), and the M13
consent page serves client registration and sign-in (FR-MCP-17, [ADR-0041](adr/0041-http-transport-with-oauth-2-1.md)).
- `run_event` is append-only (T1.3), so a cursor over it is stable. Pause and attention need no new run state: the FRD
run state machine is unchanged, and `needs_attention` is a derived flag (FR-CTL-03).
**Conventions (Proposed, Delegated).**

- **No new run state.** Pause holds admission; a running run finishes. Needs-attention is derived on read.
- **Closed payloads.** A proxied approval listing, a proxied decision and a sink payload carry controller-generated
fields only, never agent text, prompts, diffs or code. Agent-written text in a digest is labelled untrusted and
length-capped.
- **Operator values, not provider facts.** Budgets, N, T and the successor cap are operator settings. Their defaults are
Assumptions, recorded in the T14.0 LLD section, and no number is presented as a provider limit (ADR-0007).
- **Design gate.** T14.0 writes the contracts before code (AGENTS.md). A persistence change (`decided_via`, pause and
budget state) is covered by ADR-0047 or by an ADR written first.

*Proposed breakdown (2026-10-15, Delegated agent work, documentation only; not owner-approved), written from the M15 row
in §6.* Owner decision 51 sets the milestone and the narrowing of CAP-14. Requirements: [SRS
§3.18](requirements/SRS.md#318-project-queue-and-triggers-fr-que) (FR-QUE-01 to 03) and [PRD
CAP-16](requirements/PRD.md#3-capabilities). Each queue item reuses the admission path of `delegate_task` (FR-MCP-03)
and the dynamic-project ceiling rules (FR-PRJ-10), and the approval and ceiling rules of M14 (§6.13). The CI trigger
reads CI through the operator's `gh` CLI (owner decision 54, answering Q-91).

#### 6.16.1 Order, waves and hot files

- **Wave A (agents, on fakes):** T16.1, then T16.2, T16.3 and T16.9 after it (T16.9 also after T16.3).
- **Wave B:** T16.4 after T16.1 and T16.3; T16.5 after T16.4 once `src/adapters/**` is free (§6.8.1); T16.6 after
  T16.5; T16.7 after T16.6; T16.10 after T16.6; T16.11 after T16.6 and T16.9; T16.12 last.
- **Operator, whenever a provider is logged in:** T16.8. Native delivery stays off for a cell until its evidence
  lands; M16 `Done` does not wait for it.
- **Hot files:** `src/mcp/schemas.ts` and `src/mcp/server.ts` (T16.4, T16.9); `src/lifecycle/lifecycle.ts` (T16.4,
  T16.6); `src/adapters/prompt.ts` and `src/adapters/**` (T16.5, T16.7); `src/git/**` and `src/workspace/**` (T16.6);
  `src/config/schema.ts` and `src/config/load.ts` (T16.3); `src/ledger/migrations/` (T16.1). Tasks sharing a hot file
  run one after another, never in parallel (AGENTS.md).

## 7. Risks, blockers and open questions

### 7.1 Risks

| ID | Risk | Effect on plan | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-1 | Provider CLIs change flags, output or auth behaviour (already happened with Kimi) | Adapters break or weaken security | Version gating, conformance suites, manifests (ADR-0009) |
| R-2 | Provider terms restrict automated or third-party use for some plans | A provider may be unusable | Compliance manifest review per provider; each user runs their own installation with their own logins (ADR-0003, ADR-0011) |
| R-11 | Publishing as open source invites users to run Switchboard in ways the terms do not allow (shared logins, hosted service) | Account risk for those users; reputational risk for the project | README states the single-operator model and that terms compliance is each user's responsibility (NFR-COMP-01, NFR-MAINT-03) |

| Q-73 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the orchestrator, Linus, for T13.3; not owner-approved).* What form do the embedded authorization server's tokens take, and how are they stored and checked? Access and refresh tokens are opaque random values of at least 256 bits from a CSPRNG, never JWTs. Only a SHA-256 hash of each token is stored, in the ledger (forward-only migration 0010, `oauth_token`), with client, audience, scopes, expiry and a revoked flag; lookup is by hash with a constant-time compare. Unknown, expired, revoked, wrong-audience and malformed tokens all get the same 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming the protected-resource metadata; only a reason code is logged. Applied in [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13) and an as-built note in [ADR-0041](adr/0041-http-transport-with-oauth-2-1.md) item 5. | — |
| Q-74 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's T13.\* instruction to pick the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved, no bypass effect).* How open is Dynamic Client Registration (ADR-0041 item 3)? | **Decided:** open registration (no initial access token, so the Grok Bot embed can register itself), but public clients only (no secret), `https` redirect URIs only (plain `http`, loopback included, refused until a native client needs it), the authorization-code grant with optional refresh only, and every new client `pending` with no grant until the operator approves it on the consent page. At most 16 pending clients from the last 24 hours (**Assumption**), a 16 KiB body cap (**Assumption**); `scope` and other unknown fields are ignored. [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13), FR-MCP-16. Revisit if a client needs a loopback redirect or the cap is too tight. |
| Q-75 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the orchestrator, Linus, for T13.8; not owner-approved).* How is the consent-page passphrase hashed without a new dependency? | **Decided:** no new npm dependency, native or not. Node's built-in `crypto.argon2` exists in Node 24 (checked on 24.21.0) but not in Node 22, the bottom of `engines` (`>=22`) and the version CI pins, so ADR-0041's argon2id is replaced by the built-in scrypt with N=2^17, r=8, p=1, a 16-byte random salt and a 32-byte key, compared with `timingSafeEqual`. The hash (`scrypt$17$8$1$<salt>$<key>`) is the only form `transport.http.passphrase_hash` accepts; `switchboard consent hash-passphrase` prints it from a passphrase read on stdin. As-built note in [ADR-0041](adr/0041-http-transport-with-oauth-2-1.md) item 3; [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13). Revisit when the supported Node range starts at a version with a stable `crypto.argon2`. |
| Q-76 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's T13.8 instruction to pick the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved, no bypass effect).* How do the authorization endpoint, consent page and token endpoint behave? | **Decided:** PKCE `S256` only (a missing method is `plain` and refused); `redirect_uri` and `resource` required at `/authorize` and exact; the only grantable scope is `mcp`, so `privileged` and every other scope get `invalid_scope`; no login session, so every authorization needs the passphrase or a pairing code; a pending client is approved by the first successful consent, a denied or revoked one is refused; "Deny" needs no credential and changes no status. Errors redirect only for an approved client (no open redirector through a self-registered URI). CSRF: server-side request id and token, a `__Host-` `SameSite=Strict` cookie, the issuer's own `Origin` only and no cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site`. Five wrong passphrases in 15 minutes lock passphrase approval for 15 minutes, even for the right passphrase; one scrypt check at a time. Wrong pairing codes are throttled separately (ten a minute) and never locked, so a stranger who holds the passphrase lockout cannot also block the operator's recovery by pairing code (an attacker can still delay passphrase approval; accepted as the fail-closed cost). Pairing codes: 60 bits, hashed, single use, 10 minutes, a new one ends older ones. Codes: in memory, hashed, single use, 60 seconds; a reused code revokes the client's tokens. Access tokens 15 minutes, refresh tokens 7 days and rotated (checks before the token is spent), a reused refresh token revokes the client's tokens (lifetimes and limits are **Assumptions**). The pairing command is `switchboard consent pair`, not ADR-0041's `auth pair`, because FR-OPS-03 and its test forbid an `auth` command. **For zemdregon (not blocking):** FR-OPS-03 says "no web interface", and the consent page that ADR-0041 (Q-67) requires is one; this task read ADR-0041 as the narrower, later decision. The orchestrator (Linus) confirmed that reading on 2026-10-14 (Delegated, not owner-approved), and FR-OPS-03 now names the consent page as its one exception. [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13), FR-MCP-17. |
| Q-77 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's T13.\* instruction to pick the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; no bypass effect: privileged runs over HTTP still need the operator's approval, and bypass stays an approved-scope matter).* How does an authenticated HTTP client map to a configured MCP client, and how is the MCP server mounted? | **Decided:** the token subject is the OAuth client id; `transport.http.clients` maps it to an `mcp_clients` id, and `default_mcp_client` (operator opt-in) covers approved clients with no mapping; with neither the request gets 403 `insufficient_scope`, as does a token without the `mcp` scope. Config load refuses an unknown target, a target with `privileged_approval: not_required`, so no remote client can skip the operator's privileged approval (FR-MCP-14), and a `default_mcp_client` with a `privileged` ceiling (only an explicit per-client mapping may reach one). Each request re-checks that the OAuth client is still approved. Only `POST` is served; 16 requests in flight, 4 per OAuth client and a 256 KiB body (**Assumptions**); the `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers are removed before the MCP layer. The mount is the SDK's stateless Streamable HTTP mode: a fresh server and transport per request, JSON responses, no session ID ever issued or accepted, so a session cannot authenticate on its own (FR-MCP-15). OAuth clients mapped to the same entry share its runs (**Assumption**: acceptable for a single operator; superseded by Q-78, which binds them per OAuth client). [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13). Revisit if a client needs server-sent notifications (stateful sessions, T13.5). |
| Q-78 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's T13.5 instruction to decide fail-closed; not owner-approved; no bypass effect: it only narrows who can see a run).* What does FR-MCP-15's "session bound to the subject and client" mean on a stateless HTTP mount (Q-77)? | **Decided:** there is no MCP session, so a request carrying an `Mcp-Session-Id` header is refused (400) rather than ignored. What a caller comes back to is a meta-session and its runs, so those are bound: each meta-session opened over HTTP is recorded with the token's OAuth client (`http_subject`, migration 0013, the one ledger change) right after admission, and a run belongs to its meta-session (retry successors included). It is known only to its own configured MCP client and subject: over HTTP the binding must name the caller's OAuth client, over stdio there must be none. Anything else gets the "unknown id" answer of an id that does not exist (no existence oracle; not LLD's earlier 403); another subject's idempotency key reads as a key reused with different parameters. A crash between admission and the binding write leaves the meta-session stdio-only, which fails closed for HTTP callers. The serve log is redacted at the boundary, and the redactor now matches Switchboard's own token and code prefixes. Not bound: dynamic projects (T9.9), which stay per MCP client (**Assumption**), and no audit event is written for a refused lookup (it is indistinguishable from a typo). [LLD §3.3](design/LLD.md#33-network-mcp-transport-m13), FR-MCP-15. Revisit if stateful sessions (server-sent notifications) are ever needed. |
| Q-79 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's M4 instruction to choose the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; it compiles the bypass cell owner decision 46 asks for and restricts nothing a bypass run could do before).* How does the Cursor adapter compile an approved `privileged` bypass scope (T4.42), given that `--sandbox enabled` exits 1 on the operator's host and what `--force` does to the sandbox was never observed (T4.41 rows 9 and 16)? | **Decided:** `cursor-agent --print --output-format stream-json --trust --force`, prompt on stdin, no `--sandbox` flag, and only for worktree files, shell `broad`, network `on` and repository configuration `enabled` with no requested model. Every narrower scope is `Ineligible: CAPABILITY_MISSING`, because without a sandbox Cursor enforces no read-only files, no shell limit and no network limit, and `--trust` (needed to start) loads the repository's rules; claiming any of those would claim a control that is not enforced. Cursor confines nothing in this run: what remains is the controller's worktree as working directory, the tool-call guard (ADR-0039), FR-GIT-03 and FR-GIT-06. Revisit when an operator capture shows `--sandbox enabled` confining under `--force` on a host where it starts (then network `off` and read-only files could compile with it). [TDD §4.5.1](design/TDD.md#451-cursor-native-controls-per-profile-and-platform-t440) "Today" row |
| Q-80 | *Delegated, answered by the orchestrator (2026-10-14, T7.0; not zemdregon, no bypass effect; [ADR-0044](adr/0044-deterministic-route-scoring-and-replayable-decisions.md)).* What values do the FR-RTE-02 score terms and weights take when no source gives a provider's price, model ranking or sandbox strength? | **Decided:** `security` and `cost` are 0.5 for every candidate (they never decide a route); `success`, `latency` and `handoff` come from the controller's ledger; an unknown capacity estimate scores 0, never headroom (Q-69); every weight defaults to 1 (**Assumption**), configurable 0 to 100; with no history the configured order decides, as in M2. [LLD §17.3](design/LLD.md#173-score-fr-rte-02) |
| Q-81 | *Delegated, answered by the orchestrator (2026-10-14, T7.0; not zemdregon, no bypass effect).* The affinity points LLD §3.2 leaves open: thresholds, when the row is written, continuations, expiry. | **Decided (fail closed, keep the provider):** `low_water_mark` and `min_confidence` default to `null`, so only positive evidence (known quota exhaustion, a `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` run, an exhausted retry chain) switches; the row is written only when a run whose decision applied affinity succeeds (a failed first run creates none); `continue_task` decisions never move it (the quota failover successor does, as `capacity_exhausted`); `idle_ttl` accepts only `null` (Q-52). [LLD §17.6](design/LLD.md#176-affinity-details-fills-32) |
| Q-82 | *Delegated, answered by the orchestrator (2026-10-14, T7.0; not zemdregon, no bypass effect).* What does the FR-RTE-04 heuristic classifier read, and do its features change routes? | **Decided:** the request only (objective, counts of constraints and verification commands, whether the profile writes), with fixed thresholds and keyword lists (**Assumptions**, `heuristic.v1`); no repository metadata in M7. The features are recorded with `source: "heuristic"` but rank nothing, because no source maps a feature to a provider's fitness. [LLD §17.2](design/LLD.md#172-heuristic-features-fr-rte-04) |
| Q-83 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's M4 instruction to choose the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; it compiles the bypass cell owner decision 46 asks for).* How does the OpenCode adapter compile an approved `privileged` bypass scope (T4.52), given that no per-run permission set took effect on v2.0.23 (Q-64) and that its default already runs shell commands and edits without asking? | **Decided:** `opencode run --format json --standalone -- <prompt>` with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1`, and only for worktree files, shell `broad`, network `on` and repository configuration `enabled` with no requested model; every narrower scope is `Ineligible: CAPABILITY_MISSING`, since nothing enforces it. `--auto` stays declared bypass-class but is **not** emitted: the cell is reachable without it, and it would only approve what the default refuses (reads and writes outside the working directory, live check row 11), so leaving it out is the least privilege that still runs. `--standalone` is always emitted, because without it the tools run in the host's shared background service, outside the run's process group, environment allowlist, timeouts and cancel. OpenCode confines nothing in this run: what remains is the controller's worktree as working directory, the tool-call guard (ADR-0039), FR-GIT-03 and FR-GIT-06. Revisit if a headless `ask` is ever seen to hang a bypass run (then `--auto` may be needed), or when a per-run deny is shown to hold. [TDD §4.6.1](design/TDD.md#461-opencode-native-controls-per-profile-and-platform-t450) "Today" row |
| Q-84 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's M4 instruction to choose the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; it compiles the bypass cell owner decision 46 asks for).* How does the Antigravity adapter compile an approved `privileged` bypass scope (T4.32), given that `toolPermission` is a settings value and that whether `--sandbox` or deny rules still hold under `--dangerously-skip-permissions` was not observed (T4.31 C8)? | **Decided:** `agy --prompt=<prompt> --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions` with `AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true`, and only for worktree files, shell `broad`, network `on` and repository configuration `enabled` with no requested model; every narrower scope is `Ineligible: CAPABILITY_MISSING`, since nothing shown enforces it, and `--sandbox` is not compiled so that no confinement is claimed. Antigravity confines nothing in this run: what remains is the controller's worktree as working directory, the tool-call guard (ADR-0039), FR-GIT-03 and FR-GIT-06. The one-dash spelling of each bypass-class flag is declared to the audit ([ADR-0045](adr/0045-one-dash-long-bypass-flag-spellings.md)). Revisit when T4.38 records what `--sandbox` does under the bypass flag. [TDD §4.4.2](design/TDD.md#442-antigravity-native-controls-per-profile-and-platform-t430) "Today" row |
| Q-85 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's M4 instruction to choose the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; no bypass effect).* When is an OpenCode run a success (T4.53), given that the T4.51 live check saw correct answers exit 0 with no `step_finish` (TDD §4.6.4, contradiction 12)? | **Decided:** only a clean expected exit with a `step_finish` whose `part.reason` is `stop` and no `error` event is a success; a run that exits 0 with text but no `stop` ends `OUTPUT_PROTOCOL_ERROR`. Some good runs will fail (the live check saw the missing `step_finish` intermittently); that is the fail-closed cost, since exit 0 alone also follows a run cut short after a tool step ([I-38661], [I-27697] in TDD §4.6). Revisit when a capture shows a reliable terminal marker. [TDD §4.6](design/TDD.md#46-opencode-m4) "Success rule" row |
| Q-86 | *Answered 2026-10-14 (Delegated by the worker under the orchestrator's M4 instruction to choose the safer, fail-closed option; not owner-approved; no bypass effect).* What makes an Antigravity run a success, and is `--conversation <id>` resume compiled (T4.33), given that a soft denial, a print timeout and an unknown conversation id all exit 0 with `status` `SUCCESS` (T4.31 C7, C9, C10)? | **Decided:** success needs a clean expected exit, a `result` with `status` `SUCCESS`, a reported `total_tokens` above 0 (a print timeout reported zero usage) and no `denied_actions` entry or `error` text; anything else fails. Resume is **not** compiled: an unknown id silently starts a new conversation, so a continuation that lost its history would look like one that kept it, and only a stderr warning (not passed to the adapter) says otherwise. Revisit when a capture shows a structured marker of a resumed conversation (for example a `num_turns` that counts earlier turns, seen in C9 but not yet a documented contract). [TDD §4.4.1](design/TDD.md#441-antigravity-output-shapes-and-exit-codes-t430) |
| Q-90 | *Delegated, answered by the orchestrator (2026-10-14, T7.5; not zemdregon, no bypass effect).* FR-RTE-08 asks to reuse a project's last model; should the remembered model be passed to the adapter's `compile`? | **Decided (fail closed, keep the provider):** not yet. The model each run's native session reported is remembered in `project_affinity.model` and shown by `explain_route`, but not passed to `compile`, because the Codex adapter refuses any model (`CAPABILITY_MISSING`) and no adapter declares that a reported model id is accepted by its model flag; pinning could make a held provider ineligible. T7.12 adds pinning once adapters declare it. (Numbered Q-90, not the next free number, because the parallel M4 work takes consecutive numbers.) [LLD §17.6](design/LLD.md#176-affinity-details-fills-32) |
