| Q-95 | *Opened 2026-10-15 by T4.62 (Delegated agent finding, for Linus; not owner-approved).* [ADR-0049](adr/0049-kimi-code-transport-and-bypass-class.md) item 1 says the Kimi Code registry entry declares `-p` and `--prompt` as `bypassFlags`, so the argv audit refuses them outside an approved bypass run. The audit is shared by every provider (ADR-0035, `src/adapters/audit.ts`), so that declaration would refuse Claude Code's `-p` (print mode, emitted in every Claude Code run) and Antigravity's `--prompt=` (its prompt flag). Should the audit gain provider-scoped declarations (an ADR amending ADR-0035/ADR-0037, so a flag is bypass-class only in its own provider's argv), or is the Kimi compile gate alone enough for `--prompt`? | T4.62 declares `--auto`, `--plan` and `-y` (with the shared `--yolo`) and **not** `-p`/`--prompt`; the Kimi adapter emits `--prompt=` only in the approved bypass cell (pinned by `src/adapters/kimi/kimi.test.ts`), with no independent audit check. Bypass runs are unchanged |
| Q-96 | *Opened 2026-10-15 by the T11.5 post-#432 cross-check (Delegated agent finding, for Linus; not owner-approved; no bypass effect).* Every append-only ledger table is guarded by `BEFORE UPDATE` and `BEFORE DELETE` triggers ([ADR-0005](adr/0005-sqlite-ledger.md); migration 0001, recreated by 0006 for `usage_observation`). SQLite's `REPLACE` conflict resolution deletes the colliding row without firing delete triggers unless `PRAGMA recursive_triggers` is on, and `openLedger` (`src/ledger/db.ts`) leaves it off, so `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO <table>` with an existing id rewrites a guarded row. Pinned as-built in `src/inner/usage.test.ts`: a labelled `inner_agent` usage row relabelled `provider_reported` this way reaches the capacity collector's read. Not reachable from any Switchboard surface: no production module issues a `REPLACE` (the widened writer scan in the same file covers `usage_observation`; a search of the non-test modules under `src/` finds only `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` and `DO NOTHING` upserts, all on mutable tables), and ids are the ledger's own. Should `openLedger` set `recursive_triggers = ON`, one line, after which every guarded table refuses `REPLACE` too and the as-built pin is updated? Delegated best practice says yes (fail closed), but it changes the ledger opener outside the T11 lane, so it is left for Linus. **Answered 2026-10-15 by Linus (steward decision, Delegated; not owner-approved; no bypass effect):** yes, fail closed. `openLedger` (`src/ledger/db.ts`) now sets `PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON` immediately after the other opener pragmas and before migrations, so a `REPLACE` on any guarded table fires the `BEFORE DELETE` guard and aborts (the append-only intent of ADR-0005; every ledger trigger is a `RAISE(ABORT)` guard that writes nothing, so recursion changes no other trigger). Pinned in `src/ledger/ledger.test.ts` (the pragma reads 1; `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO` and `REPLACE INTO` on an existing `run_event` id are refused with `append-only` and the row is byte-identical, while a `REPLACE` on the mutable `provider_health` still works) and the `src/inner/usage.test.ts` as-built pin is flipped (the relabelling `REPLACE` is refused, the labelled row is untouched and `listProviderReportedUsageSince` stays empty). All three pins fail with the pragma line removed. No other production behaviour changes; every other `Database` opener under `src/cli/` is read-only. | Set in `openLedger`; bypass runs unchanged |

## 8. Deferred and excluded work

| Item | Status | Reason | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read-only usage dashboard | Deferred | Allowed by C-2 but not needed to deliver outcomes | FR-TEL-04 |
| Upstream ACP server | Deferred | MCP satisfies C-7 | ADR-0002 |
| Learned (contextual-bandit) routing | Deferred | Needs outcome data | FR-RTE-05 |
| OpenCode persistent `serve`/`attach` transport | Deferred | `opencode run` suffices first | FR-EXE-04 |
| Native Windows host | Deferred | Linux first | NFR-PORT-03 |
| HTTP/SSE MCP transport | Superseded by M13 (Q-67, 2026-10-14) | Network Streamable HTTP is now a core priority; see ADR-0041 | ADR-0002, ADR-0041 |
| Automatic merge of result branches | Deferred | Needs judgement | ADR-0006 |
| Multi-user or hosted operation | Excluded | Compliance and credential risk | ADR-0011 |
| Context kinds other than `repository`; remote-clone contexts; multiple writable contexts in one run | Deferred | Not asked for yet; the schema is extensible | FR-PRJ-02 |
| Rewriting attribution inside file contents | Excluded | Out of the commit boundary; the controller does not edit what agents write | FR-GIT-04, R-14 |
| Model-assisted secret or PII redaction (inner agent) | Deferred | A miss is a silent leak and sending content to find secrets is itself exposure; deterministic redaction stays the control. Revisit as an add-only advisory pass on a `local` backend | FR-INN-18 |
| Inner agent exposed to orchestrators as a tool | Excluded | Makes Switchboard a model proxy and widens TB-1; no requirement behind it | ADR-0016 |
| Inner-agent tasks IT-10 to IT-14 (prompt rewriting, test selection, diff pre-review, commit splitting, changelogs) | Deferred or excluded | Each changes intent, verification or authority, or has no requirement; see [PRD §3.1](requirements/PRD.md#31-inner-agent-task-catalogue) | — |
| Token-bucket rate gate per provider at a published rate | Deferred (2026-10-14); T6.8 reopened 2026-10-17 as the pacing gate (owner decision 57) | No source publishes an enforceable rate limit for the subscription logins in use (T6.0 inventory); a bucket at an invented rate would invent a number. The pacing gate (FR-CAP-10) uses observed usage and operator-declared budgets instead | FR-CAP-07, FR-CAP-10 |
| Approximate-nearest-neighbour or vector-database index for retrieval | Deferred | The first version is SQLite with in-process search under a hard cap; revisit only if the T12.0 spike shows the cap is too low | FR-RAG-01, Q-48 |
| Learned reranking of retrieved snippets | Deferred | No measurement yet that retrieval helps (R-57); no requirement | — |
| Code-graph or symbol-level retrieval | Deferred | Not asked for; text chunks first | — |
| Retrieval index shared across operators or installations | Excluded | Multi-user and hosted operation are excluded; the global index is one installation's | ADR-0011, FR-RAG-09 |
| Agent subscriptions to PR and merge events (CI pass or fail, another agent's commit to the PR, merge) | Deferred (Proposed, optional; owner's words in decision 43) | Optional, after everything else in the plan. Needs PRD use case, SRS requirements and a milestone before it is built; the GitHub webhook path and its trust rules are unspecified. *(Note 2026-10-15, owner decision 51: the narrowed form, fixing CI on branches a project published, is scheduled in M15 as CAP-16 and FR-QUE-03; FR-SUB-01 stays Deferred.)* | CAP-14 (PRD §3); FR-SUB-01 (SRS §3.16, Deferred) |
| Skills written to the operator's home directory or a provider config directory | Excluded (2026-10-17, owner decision 58, Delegated reading) | Shared by every run of that provider and by the operator's own use; leaks across projects and survives a crash | FR-SKL-05, [ADR-0056](adr/0056-switchboard-controlled-skills.md) |
| Skills authored or edited by orchestrators over MCP | Deferred (Q-106) | A prompt-injected client could plant standing instructions in other projects' runs | FR-SKL-08 |
| Skills with scripts, hooks, MCP definitions or other executable assets | Excluded | A skill is text only; executable content would be a new execution path outside the trust profiles | FR-SKL-01, FR-SKL-02 |

### 9.1 How an agent picks up work

1. Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), then this roadmap's §6 to find the first milestone whose status is not `Done`. A
   `Partial` milestone is closed from its "Blocks Done" list before the next one starts, unless every remaining item
   needs the operator or zemdregon; agents then work on the next milestone's tasks that do not depend on those items (as
   M3 wave A does while M2's residual live-smoke cells stay operator-only (§6.2 "Blocks Done" item 1)).
2. Take the first task in that milestone's task table whose dependencies are done. If the milestone has no task table
   yet (M4's is §6.8, M5's §6.9, M6's §6.11, M7's §6.12, M8's §6.15, M14's §6.13 and M15's §6.14), break it into tasks in
   the same format first, from its row in §6 and the requirements it lists, and add them here before coding.
3. Read every reference in the task row: the SRS requirements, the FRD workflow or rule, the LLD/TDD section and the
   ADRs. Those are the contract; this roadmap only sequences them.
4. Implement with tests that prove the task's "Done when" checks and the cited requirements' verification method.
5. In the same change, update the task's status here with evidence, and fix any document the work proved wrong (or add
   an ADR if an architectural decision changed).
6. Run `node scripts/check-docs.mjs` and the test suite before opening the pull request.

## 10. Keeping this roadmap current

- Change status in §6 in the same change as the work, with evidence.
- New scope goes through the PRD and SRS first, then gets a milestone here.
- A conflict between documents is resolved in favour of the owner named in §5, and the losing document is corrected in
  the same change.
